bug_description.original: An overflow exists in the function bigint_monty_redc, which assumes that the variable z is 2*p_words+2 words long. The function relies on implicit rounding up in grow_to to ensure that a resize results in a sufficiently large value. This assumption can lead to incorrect memory allocation and potential security issues.
bug_description.normalized: While importing the staged 344-byte PKCS#8 witness as an ECDSA private key with explicit EC parameters, Botan decodes an attacker-controlled field prime whose meaningful bytes fit in one 64-bit word and constructs a Montgomery curve from it. During EC_Group creation, PointGFp copies the decoded base-point affine y coordinate into `m_coord_y` as a 24-byte BigInt and immediately converts that same object to Montgomery representation. CurveGFp_Montgomery::curve_mul derives `output_size = 2*m_p_words + 1`, so with `m_p_words == 1` it accepts that existing 3-word buffer without growing it. bigint_monty_redc then computes its own required extent as `2*(p_size+1) == 4` words and reads the missing fourth word at mp_monty.cpp:62, producing the observed ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.code:
BER_Decoder(bits, len)
   .start_cons(SEQUENCE)
     .decode_and_check<size_t>(1, "Unknown ECC param version code")
     .start_cons(SEQUENCE)
      .decode_and_check(OID("1.2.840.10045.1.1"),
                        "Only prime ECC fields supported")
       .decode(p)
source.description: First project parser statement on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled EC domain state: it decodes the explicit field prime `p` from the PKCS#8 AlgorithmIdentifier parameters later reduced to `m_p_words`.
source.value_from: The exact Stage 01 witness is the 344-byte file `gt_results/arvo_6581/poc` (SHA-256 `5c7772f831149c76afcb9243d60b179300cca571b1715b18351a524710bd092e`). The saved run reaches `EC_Group::BER_decode_EC_group`, takes the explicit-parameters SEQUENCE branch, and decodes a prime INTEGER whose non-zero tail bytes are `ff ff ff ff ff 00 00 01`, i.e. one significant 64-bit word on this build.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This constructor reduces the attacker-controlled prime to the size driver `m_p_words`. On the crashing path, `m_p_words == 1`, and every later output-size calculation in the vulnerable Montgomery path derives from that single tainted word count.

sink.description: ASan crash site. bigint_monty_redc treats `z` as a 4-word buffer and reads the nonexistent fourth word while propagating carry through the high limbs.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 8` at this line on address `0x603000008f98`, immediately to the right of the 24-byte heap region allocated by `m_coord_y(y)` in `PointGFp::PointGFp` at point_gfp.cpp:32.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable size formula underestimates the Montgomery reduction buffer by one word. bigint_monty_redc requires `2*(p_size+1)` words, but curve_mul derives only `2*m_p_words+1` and relies on a later grow_to side effect that is not guaranteed to run.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch changes this path to `2*m_p_words + 2` and makes the analogous correction in the Montgomery square and NIST helper paths. In the vulnerable code, if the incoming `m_coord_y` object already has 3 words, the `< output_size` guard is false, `grow_to(3)` is never called, and the implicit round-up never happens.

parser_admitted.description: The witness does not use a named-curve OID. Botan enters the explicit-parameters SEQUENCE branch and therefore decodes attacker-controlled `p`, `a`, `b`, `base_pt`, `order`, and `cofactor` instead of looking up a hardcoded safe curve.

algorithm_selected.description: The PKCS#8 AlgorithmIdentifier resolves to the ECDSA loader, which is why the attacker-controlled explicit EC parameters reach `EC_PrivateKey` and `EC_Group`.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact 344-byte witness in `poc` is wrapped in `DataSource_Memory` and passed to Botan's PKCS#8 loader; Stage 01 reproduced the crash on this single input.

fine_trace.code:
BER_Decoder(bits, len)
   .start_cons(SEQUENCE)
     .decode_and_check<size_t>(1, "Unknown ECC param version code")
     .start_cons(SEQUENCE)
      .decode_and_check(OID("1.2.840.10045.1.1"),
                        "Only prime ECC fields supported")
       .decode(p)
fine_trace.note: Source. In the explicit EC-parameters branch, Botan decodes the attacker-controlled field prime `p`. The witness pads this INTEGER with many leading zero bytes but its non-zero tail is `ff ff ff ff ff 00 00 01`, so the resulting BigInt has one significant 64-bit word.

The same explicit-parameters blob also supplies the encoded base point bytes that Botan later converts into affine coordinates; the crashing value path follows the resulting `base_xy.second` object into `m_coord_y`.

fine_trace.code: std::pair<BigInt, BigInt> base_xy = Botan::OS2ECP(base_pt.data(), base_pt.size(), p, a, b);
fine_trace.note: Botan converts the attacker-controlled encoded base point into affine coordinates `base_xy.first` and `base_xy.second`. The later overread follows `base_xy.second`, which `EC_Group_Data` passes as `g_y` into PointGFp storage.

Because the decoded prime is not one of Botan's hardcoded NIST primes, curve construction falls through to the Montgomery representation. The saved crash stack later confirms execution in `CurveGFp_Montgomery::curve_mul` rather than a named-curve reducer.

Tainted size origin. The chosen prime collapses to `m_p_words == 1` on this 64-bit build, and all later buffer-size arithmetic in the vulnerable Montgomery path derives from that single attacker-controlled word count.

EC_Group_Data constructs the base point and copies `base_xy.second` into `m_coord_y`. The saved ASan allocation stack attributes the later-overread 24-byte region to this copy at point_gfp.cpp:32, so the crashing `m_coord_y` backing store is exactly 3 words.

The saved crash stack hits this call at point_gfp.cpp:42. `CurveGFp_Montgomery::to_curve_rep` immediately forwards the same `m_coord_y` BigInt by reference into `curve_mul`, so this 24-byte object becomes the `z` buffer on the crashing path.

Root cause. With `m_p_words == 1`, `curve_mul` computes `output_size == 3` for the incoming `m_coord_y` buffer now bound to `z`. However `bigint_monty_redc` is specified for `2*(p_size+1)` words, so this same modulus actually requires 4 words.

The copied `m_coord_y` BigInt already has `z.size() == 3`, so the `< output_size` guard is false and `grow_to` never runs. Since `grow_to` only rounds up when `n > size()` (`bigint.cpp:291-299`), the expected implicit expansion does not happen and `z` remains the observed 24-byte / 3-word `m_coord_y` allocation.
curve_mul propagates that same 3-word `m_coord_y` object as `z` into Montgomery multiplication and reduction while also passing `p_size == m_p_words == 1`.

Inside reduction, the same modulus size is reinterpreted as a required buffer length of `z_size == 4` words. That is one word larger than the current 3-word `m_coord_y` / `z` allocation forwarded by curve_mul.

Sink. With `i == 0`, `p_size == 1`, and `z_size == 4`, the carry-propagation loop at lines 60-64 iterates `j = 2, 3`; the `j == 3` iteration reads the missing fourth word `z_i[3]` just beyond the 24-byte `m_coord_y` allocation from step 7. ASan reports the resulting 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at this line.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved allocation stack points to `m_coord_y(y)` at point_gfp.cpp:32, the crash stack points to `m_curve.to_rep(m_coord_y, monty_ws)` at point_gfp.cpp:42, and step 9 follows that same `m_coord_y` BigInt into `CurveGFp_Montgomery::curve_mul` as `z`.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is the `m_coord_y` copy at point_gfp.cpp:32 later reused as `z` from point_gfp.cpp:42; the root cause is the separate under-allocation formula in `CurveGFp_Montgomery::curve_mul`.

poc.trigger: Feed the exact 344-byte witness in `poc` to the staged `pkcs8` libFuzzer target. Stage 01 reproduced an ASan heap-buffer-overflow read in `bigint_monty_redc` during that single-input run.

format.name: BER/DER PKCS#8 ECDSA private key
format.contract: The crashing witness is a single 344-byte PKCS#8 `PrivateKeyInfo` whose `AlgorithmIdentifier` uses explicit EC parameters (SEQUENCE, not a named-curve OID). Its field-prime INTEGER decodes to one significant 64-bit word (`... ff ff ff ff ff 00 00 01`), Botan therefore chooses `CurveGFp_Montgomery`, and the base-point affine y coordinate copied into `m_coord_y` during `PointGFp` construction arrives at `curve_mul` with a 3-word backing store. That exact combination makes the vulnerable `output_size = 2*m_p_words+1` path leave `z` one word short for `bigint_monty_redc`.
